output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: spark.staticfiles.DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainstForExternal / protectAgainstInClassPath validated the resolved path with removeLeadingAndTrailingSlashesFrom(path).startsWith(root). startsWith matches on raw string prefix, so a sibling folder like 'pub-secret' passes the check for root 'pub'. Combined with UriPath.canonical missing backslash separators (cleanPath later converts '\' to '/' and collapses '..'), an attacker could resolve files outside the configured root.

Fix: introduced private isContainedWithin(path, root) that returns true only when path.equals(root) or path.startsWith(root + "/") (root==null -> reject, root empty -> allow, preserving the '/'-configured-root behavior). Both guard methods now use it. This is a focused, defense-in-depth hardening of the existing runtime check with no API changes.

Tests: added DirectoryTraversalTest covering (1) a legitimate file inside the configured external folder is accepted, (2) a sibling folder sharing the root as a prefix is rejected (the bypass), and (3) an absolute outside path is rejected. Existing StaticFilesTest (includes local traversal protection) and StaticFilesTestExternal continue to pass.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. Change only tightens the containment check; legitimate paths equal to the root or below it with a '/' boundary are still accepted, verified by StaticFilesTest/StaticFilesTestExternal. Behavior for an empty root (folder configured as '/') is preserved (allow-all). Only theoretical behavior change is rejecting the previously-accepted prefix-sibling case, which is the intended security fix. No dependency or API changes.
output_json.summary: Fixed a path-traversal bypass in the static-file DirectoryTraversal guard. The guard re-resolves a served resource's absolute path and confirms it is inside the configured static-files root, but it used a naive startsWith string-prefix check. That let a resolved path escape into a sibling directory whose name shares the root as a string prefix (e.g. root /tmp/pub accepting /tmp/pub-secret/passwd). Because UriPath.canonical only normalizes '/', backslash-based traversal slips past canonicalization and this guard is the last defense, so the prefix flaw was exploitable. Replaced the raw startsWith with an isContainedWithin helper requiring the path to equal the root or continue with a '/' boundary, applied to both the external and classpath guards.
